chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ibn Asbaat, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The seventh pillar, from what faces the doors of Kinda in the courtyard, is the place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the fifth is the place of Jibraeel (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: Which pillars in the Grand Mosque of Kufa are associated with Prophet Ibrahim and Angel Jibraeel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* locates the spiritual presence of Prophet Ibrahim and the Angel Jibraeel within specific pillars of the Grand Mosque of Kufa’s courtyard, linking the site to the legacy of the Kaaba. In Shia tradition, these 'Maqams' serve as focal points for *ziyarat* and prayer, emphasizing the continuity of sacred geography from Mecca to Kufa. The identification underscores the theological view that Kufa holds a status akin to the holiest sites, inviting worshippers to emulate the devotion of the Prophets and Angels.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ibn Asbaat, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The seventh pillar is from what follows the doors of Kinda in the courtyard, being a place of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, and the fifth place of Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl from ibn Asbat in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the seventh pillar counting from Kindah doors in the compound is the station of Ibrahim and the fifth is the station of Jibril (Gabriel), Allah has granted him peace.”
